problem: writeExportFile swallows any mkdir/writeFile failure (logged only when KERYX_VERBOSE is set) and resolves normally. Its only caller, runHistoryExport (line 122), then prints `exported N run(s) to <file>` and leaves exitCode 0. A failed write (unwritable directory, target is a directory, disk full) is reported as success. Violates error-handling.mdc Rule 3 / Iron Law 1. Class scope: the new file has two other catches (line 34 rethrows, line 127 is a commented display-only fallback); this one is the only silent one.
impact: A user or a script attaching the export to a review or flow journal is told the file was written and gets exit 0, then finds no file or a stale one from an earlier run.

problem: The collectRunRows doc comment says it returns the runs oldest first, but it only filters listWikiRuns, which is documented and implemented as newest first (src/wiki/history.ts:495, 508 sort descending). Nothing reverses the order, so the exported file reads newest first.
impact: The next reader trusts the comment about export order; anyone relying on chronological order in the exported file (as the comment promises) gets reverse order.
quote:
Returns the runs

problem: The catch rethrows a new Error without `{ cause: error }` (the caught `error` is unused) and the message does not say which runs log or cwd failed. error-handling.mdc Rules 2 and 5 / Iron Law 3.
impact: Whoever debugs a failed export loses the original errno/stack (EACCES vs. corrupt file) and the path that failed.
quote: throw new Error("wiki history: could not read the runs log");

problem: The command-label normalization chain (collapse newlines, collapse whitespace, trim, slice to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH) is copied three times: wiki-history-export.ts:49-53, wiki-history-export.ts:56-60, and wiki-history.ts:47-51. It should be one exported helper (e.g. formatCommandLabel) next to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH.
impact: Any change to how labels are cleaned or clipped must be made in three places in two files; the terminal view and the two export formats will drift.

problem: renderRunLine takes four positional parameters including a boolean flag `markdown` that selects two entirely different renderings, and `pages` duplicates `run.pages` (the only caller passes `run.pages`, line 119). Split into renderCsvLine/renderMarkdownLine (or dispatch on RunExportFormat) taking the run and the display timestamp.
impact: Call sites read `renderRunLine(run, at, run.pages, format === "md")`; the boolean and redundant argument must be decoded from the signature, and a third format means another flag.

problem: runHistoryExport is about 57 lines and does several separable jobs at different levels: argument validation, format inference from the extension, --since date parsing (regex + Date construction), collection, row rendering with timestamp trimming, file I/O, and realpath-based display. Format resolution and --since parsing should be pure helpers returning a value or an error.
impact: The parsing rules cannot be unit-tested without invoking the whole command and touching the filesystem; each new option grows this function further.

problem: HISTORY_USAGE documents the export as `[--export <file> [--format csv|md]]` and omits `--since` and `--command`, while EXPORT_USAGE (wiki-history-export.ts:13) and the wiki.ts help text list all four. Two usage strings in the same diff describe one command differently.
impact: A user who reads this usage line never learns the filters exist; the strings will keep drifting as options are added.
